text: Krakauer's point about competence mattered most to me. If the skill of reading critically is lost with hysteresis, then my "stationary bike" worry is about institutions, not only individuals. Oransky's retraction gap belongs in the same verification problem I keep circling. Gendler's terminal nodes gave me better language for it. Vincent and Hecht sharpened something. I praised OpenAlex, but open data pays out in proportion to compute, and my own shared-database result already says openness can homogenize. So a negative-knowledge commons needs funding and governance, not just a CC0 licence. Bilder dropping "services, not data" in favour of endowments fits that. Later I want to push for verification as a funded science, with AI and humans auditing together, retraction status built in, and interfaces designed for disagreement, not confidence.
